audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for centurion servant, widow's son at Nain, John question, Jesus' witness to John, wisdom/children saying, and anointing woman with release/love/trust.

verses.restored: After he completed all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.

familiar.text: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

modern.text: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.

original.text: ⸀Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

verses.restored: A certain centurion's servant, who was precious to him, was sick and about to die.

familiar.text: And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.

modern.text: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.

original.text: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.

verses.restored: Hearing about Jesus, he sent elders of the Judeans to him, asking him to come and save/heal his servant.

familiar.text: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.

modern.text: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Coming to Jesus, they appealed earnestly to him, saying, He is worthy for you to grant this,

familiar.text: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

modern.text: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,

original.text: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ ⸀παρέξῃ τοῦτο,

verses.restored: for he loves our nation and built the synagogue for us.

familiar.text: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

modern.text: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”

original.text: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.

verses.restored: Jesus went with them. Already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying, Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not sufficient that you should enter under my roof.

familiar.text: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:

modern.text: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς. ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν ⸂φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης⸃ λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ⸂ἱκανός εἰμι⸃ ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·

verses.restored: Therefore I did not consider myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and let my servant be healed.

familiar.text: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

modern.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

original.text: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν· ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ⸀ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου·

verses.restored: For I also am a person set under authority, having soldiers under me; I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.

familiar.text: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

modern.text: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπʼ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.

verses.restored: Hearing these things, Jesus marveled at him, and turning to the crowd following him, said, I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such trust.

familiar.text: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

modern.text: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸀οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.

verses.restored: Those who had been sent returned to the house and found the servant healthy.

familiar.text: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.

modern.text: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health. Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son

original.text: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες ⸂εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες⸃ εὗρον ⸀τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.

verses.restored: Soon afterward he went to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a great crowd went with him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

modern.text: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ⸀ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.

verses.restored: As he drew near the gate of the city, look, one who had died was being carried out, an only son of his mother; she was a widow, and a considerable crowd from the city was with her.

familiar.text: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

modern.text: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς ⸂μονογενὴς υἱὸς⸃ τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ⸀ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ⸁ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.

verses.restored: Seeing her, the Lord was moved with compassion for her and said to her, Do not weep.

familiar.text: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

modern.text: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”

original.text: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μὴ κλαῖε.

verses.restored: Coming near, he touched the bier, and those carrying it stood still. He said, Young man, I say to you, rise.

familiar.text: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

modern.text: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”

original.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν· Νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.

verses.restored: The dead one sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.

familiar.text: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

modern.text: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.

original.text: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Fear seized all, and they glorified the Divine, saying, A great prophet has been raised among us, and the Divine has visited his people.

familiar.text: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.

modern.text: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”

original.text: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ⸀ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: This word about him went out in all Judea and all the surrounding region.

familiar.text: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.

modern.text: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region. John’s Inquiry (Matthew 11:1–6)

original.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.

verses.restored: John's disciples reported to him concerning all these things.

familiar.text: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.

modern.text: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.

original.text: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων. καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης

verses.restored: Calling two of his disciples, John sent them to the Lord, saying, Are you the coming one, or should we expect another?

familiar.text: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

modern.text: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”

original.text: ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ⸀κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ⸀ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

verses.restored: The men came to him and said, John the Baptist sent us to you, saying, Are you the coming one, or should we expect another?

familiar.text: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

modern.text: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”

original.text: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ⸀ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

verses.restored: In that hour he healed many from diseases, afflictions, and harmful spirits, and gifted sight to many blind people.

familiar.text: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.

modern.text: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.

original.text: ἐν ⸀ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ⸀ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.

verses.restored: Answering, he said to them, Go report to John what you saw and heard: blind people see again, lame people walk, those with skin disease are cleansed, deaf people hear, dead people are raised, poor people receive good news.

familiar.text: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

modern.text: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· ⸀τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται, ⸀κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing is whoever is not caused to stumble in me.

familiar.text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

modern.text: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me. ” Jesus Testifies about John (Malachi 3:1–5; Matthew 11:7–19)

original.text: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.

verses.restored: When John's messengers had gone away, he began to speak to the crowds concerning John: What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed shaken by wind?

familiar.text: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

modern.text: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

original.text: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν ⸂πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους⸃ περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;

verses.restored: But what did you go out to see? A person clothed in soft garments? Look, those in glorious clothing and luxury are in royal palaces.

familiar.text: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.

modern.text: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.

original.text: ἀλλὰ τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.

verses.restored: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.

familiar.text: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

modern.text: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

original.text: ἀλλὰ τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; προφήτην; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.

verses.restored: This is the one about whom it has been written: Look, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.

familiar.text: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

modern.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.

verses.restored: I say to you, among those born of women, no one is greater than John; yet the smaller one in the reign of the Divine is greater than he.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

modern.text: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

original.text: ⸀λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν ⸀Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

verses.restored: All the people hearing, and the tax collectors, justified the Divine, having been baptized with John's baptism.

familiar.text: And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

modern.text: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.

original.text: (καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·

verses.restored: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of the Divine for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

familiar.text: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.

modern.text: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.

original.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.)

verses.restored: To what then shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?

familiar.text: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

modern.text: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?

original.text: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;

verses.restored: They are like children sitting in a marketplace and calling to one another: We piped to you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not weep.

familiar.text: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.

modern.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’

original.text: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ⸂ἃ λέγει⸃· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ⸀ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·

verses.restored: For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, He has an unclean spirit.

familiar.text: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.

modern.text: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’

original.text: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ⸀μὴ ⸂ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον⸃, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·

verses.restored: The Son of Humanity has come eating and drinking, and you say, Look, a glutton and wine-drinker, friend of tax collectors and sinners/misaligned ones.

familiar.text: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!

modern.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

original.text: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.

verses.restored: Yet wisdom is justified by all her children.

familiar.text: But wisdom is justified of all her children.

modern.text: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.” A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus (Matthew 26:6–13; Mark 14:3–9; John 12:1–8)

original.text: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ ⸂πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς⸃.

verses.restored: One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him. Entering the Pharisee's house, he reclined.

familiar.text: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.

modern.text: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.

original.text: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετʼ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς ⸂τὸν οἶκον⸃ τοῦ Φαρισαίου ⸀κατεκλίθη.

verses.restored: Look, a woman in the city, who was a sinner/misaligned woman, learning that he reclined in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.

familiar.text: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,

modern.text: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ⸂ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει⸃ ἁμαρτωλός, ⸀καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι ⸀κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου

verses.restored: Standing behind at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with tears, wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

familiar.text: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

modern.text: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.

original.text: καὶ στᾶσα ⸂ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ⸃ κλαίουσα, ⸂τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.

verses.restored: Seeing this, the Pharisee who invited him said within himself, If this one were a prophet, he would know who and what sort of woman is touching him, that she is a sinner/misaligned one.

familiar.text: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.

modern.text: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”

original.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ⸀ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, Simon, I have something to say to you. He said, Teacher, say it.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Master, say on.

modern.text: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν. ὁ δέ· ⸂Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν⸃.

verses.restored: A certain lender had two debtors; one owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty.

familiar.text: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

modern.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

original.text: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.

verses.restored: When they had nothing to pay, he freely forgave both. Which of them, then, will love him more?

familiar.text: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?

modern.text: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”

original.text: μὴ ⸀ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο. τίς οὖν ⸀αὐτῶν πλεῖον ⸂ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν⸃;

verses.restored: Simon answered, I suppose the one for whom he freely forgave more. He said to him, You judged rightly.

familiar.text: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.

modern.text: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.

original.text: ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.

verses.restored: Turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she wet my feet with tears and wiped them with her hair.

familiar.text: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.

modern.text: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.

original.text: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα; εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ ⸀μοι ἐπὶ ⸀πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς ⸀θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.

verses.restored: You gave me no kiss, but from the time I entered, she has not stopped kissing my feet.

familiar.text: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

modern.text: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.

original.text: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφʼ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.

verses.restored: You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed my feet with ointment.

familiar.text: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.

modern.text: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.

original.text: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν ⸂τοὺς πόδας μου⸃.

verses.restored: For this reason I say to you: her many sins/misalignments have been released, for she loved much; but the one to whom little is released loves little.

familiar.text: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

modern.text: Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”

original.text: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.

verses.restored: He said to her, Your sins/misalignments are released.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

verses.restored: Those reclining with him began to say among themselves, Who is this who even releases sins/misalignments?

familiar.text: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?

modern.text: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

original.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;

verses.restored: He said to the woman, Your trust has saved/healed you; go into peace.

familiar.text: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

modern.text: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
